## Figure 1.17: External Debt Stock to Exports of Low-Income, Middle-Income, IDA-Eligible, and Low- and Middle-Income Countries (Excluding China), 2015–25
Type: line chart

- **Unit:** Percent
- **Y-axis:** 0 to 350 percent
- **X-axis / time span:** 2015–2025
- **Series / legend:**
  - Low-income countries
  - IDA-eligible countries
  - Middle-income countries
  - Low- and middle-income countries (excl. China)

### Approximate values by series
Values are estimated from line positions because no printed point labels are shown.

| Year | Low-income countries | IDA-eligible countries | Middle-income countries | Low- and middle-income countries (excl. China) |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 2015 | ≈255 | ≈175 | ≈100 | ≈138 |
| 2016 | ≈275 | ≈190 | ≈106 | ≈144 |
| 2017 | ≈270 | ≈191 | ≈105 | ≈138 |
| 2018 | ≈245 | ≈182 | ≈103 | ≈130 |
| 2019 | ≈260 | ≈190 | ≈107 | ≈135 |
| 2020 | ≈310 | ≈248 | ≈123 | ≈165 |
| 2021 | ≈252 | ≈221 | ≈104 | ≈135 |
| 2022 | ≈214 | ≈192 | ≈91 | ≈113 |
| 2023 | ≈211 | ≈199 | ≈94 | ≈117 |
| 2024 | ≈189 | ≈186 | ≈89 | ≈113 |
| 2025 | ≈180 | ≈177 | ≈88 | ≈114 |

### Visual comparisons and trends
- **Highest throughout:** Low-income countries have the highest external debt stock-to-exports ratio in every year shown.
- **Lowest throughout:** Middle-income countries have the lowest ratio in every year shown.
- All four series **rise to a peak around 2020**, then **decline through 2025**.
- **Low-income countries** rise from about **255 percent in 2015** to a peak near **310 percent in 2020**, then fall steadily to about **180 percent in 2025**.
- **IDA-eligible countries** increase from about **175 percent in 2015** to about **248 percent in 2020**, then decline to **≈177 percent in 2025**.
- **Low- and middle-income countries (excluding China)** rise from about **138 percent in 2015** to about **165 percent in 2020**, then fall to about **114 percent in 2025**.
- **Middle-income countries** remain much lower than the other groups, moving from about **100 percent in 2015** to about **123 percent in 2020**, then down to about **88 percent in 2025**.
- By **2025**, the **low-income** and **IDA-eligible** lines nearly converge, at roughly **180 percent** and **177 percent**, respectively.
- The gap between **low-income countries** and **middle-income countries** is widest around **2020**.

**Largest to smallest in 2025:**
1. Low-income countries (≈180)
2. IDA-eligible countries (≈177)
3. Low- and middle-income countries, excl. China (≈114)
4. Middle-income countries (≈88)

**Source:** World Bank Group International Debt Statistics database.  
**Note:** IDA = International Development Association.
